title: Factory machine breakdowns (synthetic)
description: 400 factory machines, each with 8 everyday readings: temperature, vibration, oil pressure, motor current, speed, oil quality, sound level and hours since last service. The question: will this machine break down? The claim is that a Random Forest model predicts breakdowns at least 5 points more accurately than a simpler Logistic Regression model. On the usual single test it looks true. Watch what happens when the test is repeated.

suggested_claim.source_note: Illustrative claim written for this example; it is not taken from a published paper.

provenance_note: Made-up data generated with scikit-learn's make_classification; the column names and units were added for readability and do not describe real machines. It was picked from generated candidates because the claim holds on the usual test but not reliably on others (scripts/make_demo_fixture.py; search recorded in sensor_fault_synthetic.provenance.json).

title: Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic)
description: 569 tumors described by 30 numeric measurements. A public teaching dataset where a linear model is known to do well, which makes it a fair test of a claim that Random Forest is clearly better.

suggested_claim.source_note: Illustrative claim written for this example; it is not taken from a published paper.

provenance_note: Exported unmodified from scikit-learn's load_breast_cancer (UCI Machine Learning Repository). Not for clinical use.
